commitResults.messageTitle: Add Alias base class with tests
Add alias commands with two-level command parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
AddressBookParser reads only the first word as the command, but
our feature spec uses two-word commands like lias add and
lias delete.

Instead of reworking the parser to read two words, let's split
the parsing into two levels:
* AddressBookParser handles the first word (alias, contact, game)
* A new AliasCommandParser handles the second word (add, delete)

This keeps the code clean and makes it easy to add e.g
game commands later using the same pattern.

Changes:
* Add AliasCommandParser to route alias subcommands
* Add AddAliasCommand and DeleteAliasCommand (execute() is on-hold
  until Person supports aliases)
* Fix Alias equals()/hashCode() to be case-insensitive so that
  duplicate aliases are caught regardless of capitalisation

DeleteContactCommand: add y/n confirmation before deletion
commitResults.messageBody:
DeleteContactCommand deletes a contact immediately without any
confirmation.

Accidental deletions are hard to recover from, especially since the app
has no undo feature.

Let's,
* make DeleteContactCommand return a pending confirmation result with
  the contact's details instead of deleting immediately
* add awaitingConfirmation and pendingPerson fields to CommandResult
  to carry the confirmation state
* handle the y/n response in LogicManager, proceeding with deletion
  on "y"/"yes" and cancelling on "n"/"no" or invalid input
* update tests across DeleteContactCommandTest, CommandResultTest, and
  LogicManagerTest to reflect the new confirmation flow

commitResults.messageTitle: Add undo command to reverse the most recent action
commitResults.messageBody:
The app has no way to recover from accidental changes since all
commands take effect immediately with no way to reverse them.

Let's,
* add UndoableCommand interface with an undo(Model) method
* make AddContactCommand, DeleteContactCommand, EditCommand,
ClearCommand, AddGameCommand, DeleteGameCommand, AddAliasCommand,
and DeleteAliasCommand implement UndoableCommand by storing the
state needed to reverse each operation
* add UndoCommand which pops and reverses the most recent
UndoableCommand from the history stack
* maintain a commandHistory deque in LogicManager, pushing each
successful UndoableCommand and passing the deque to UndoCommand
when "undo" is typed

Some changes were uncommitted before the merge. Conflicts arised
between the new user profile feature and the undo command feature.
After conflict was resolved, execution of delete confirmation was wrong.
Test cases were added to test the feature of undo command.

Lets,
 * remove model.deletePerson() from DeleteContactCommand.execute()
so it only returns a confirmation prompt
 * add setDeletedPerson() setter to wire up undo state after confirm
 * store pendingDeleteCommand in LogicManager alongside
pendingDeletePerson
 * in handleDeleteConfirmation(), set deletedPerson on the command
and push it to commandHistory after "y" so undo works correctly

commitResults.messageTitle: Make isSamePerson case-insensitive to fix delete
commitResults.messageBody:
isSamePerson uses Name.equals() which is case-sensitive. This allows
contacts with names differing only in casing (e.g. "John Doe" and
"john doe") to coexist in the list. When a user attempts to delete by
name, only the exact-case entry is removed, leaving the other behind.

Let's,
* update isSamePerson to use equalsIgnoreCase on fullName so that
  name-based duplicate detection is case-insensitive
* add tests to DeleteContactCommandTest covering delete by lowercase,
  uppercase, and mixed-case name inputs

The isSamePerson test asserted that names differing only in case were
considered different persons. This encoded the old case-sensitive
behaviour which has since been intentionally changed.

Let's update the assertion from assertFalse to assertTrue for the
case-differing scenario, and update the comment to document that
isSamePerson now performs a case-insensitive name match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support partial keyword matching in find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's update all three search predicates to use substring matching
instead of exact word/full matching:

- NameContainsKeywordsPredicate: replace containsWordIgnoreCase with
  toLowerCase().contains() so "dav" matches "David Teo"
- GameContainsKeywordPredicate: replace equalsIgnoreCase with
  toLowerCase().contains() so "mine" matches "Minecraft"
- AliasMatchesPredicate: replace equalsIgnoreCase with
  toLowerCase().contains() so "benj" matches "BenJumpin"

Add test_partialKeyword_returnsTrue to each predicate test class,
covering partial match at start, middle, and case-insensitive.
